items.question: Is the centre known by the Local Government or able to explain its registration or licensing status?
items.action: Ask the centre manager whether the centre is registered, licensed or in the process of registration. Ask which Local Government education office knows the centre.
items.warning: A centre that refuses to discuss registration, licensing or responsible offices should be treated with caution.
items.source_label: ECCE Policy and Standards on registration, licensing and accountability

items.question: Are children supervised by responsible adults throughout the day?
items.action: Observe whether adults are present in classrooms, play areas, toilets, feeding areas and entrances.
items.warning: Children left alone or supervised by very few adults is a serious safety concern.
items.source_label: BRMS and ECCE Standards on supervision

items.question: Do caregivers speak to children warmly and respectfully?
items.action: Watch how caregivers respond when children cry, ask questions, make mistakes or need help.
items.warning: Shouting, humiliation, fear, harsh punishment or rough handling are red flags.
items.source_label: ECCE Policy guidance on nurturing care and child wellbeing

items.question: Does the centre prohibit violence, harsh punishment, neglect and unsafe discipline?
items.action: Ask how the centre disciplines children and how staff are guided on child protection.
items.warning: Be concerned if beating, isolation, threats, insults or fear are treated as normal discipline.
items.source_label: ECCE Policy and Standards on child safety and protection

items.question: Is there a safe way for parents to report concerns?
items.action: Ask who parents should contact if a child is hurt, mistreated, neglected or unsafe.
items.warning: A centre without a complaints or reporting pathway may fail to respond to harm quickly.
items.source_label: ECCE Standards on complaints and reporting

items.question: Are the buildings, classrooms and compound safe for young children?
items.action: Look for safe floors, doors, windows, fences, play areas and clear movement spaces.
items.warning: Open hazards, broken structures, unsafe water points, sharp objects or unsecured compounds need urgent attention.
items.source_label: BRMS and ECCE Standards on safety and security

items.question: Are toilets clean, accessible and suitable for young children?
items.action: Ask to see the toilets and handwashing area before enrolling or during centre visits.
items.warning: Dirty, inaccessible or unsafe toilets can expose children to illness and fear.
items.source_label: BRMS on sanitation and child-friendly facilities

items.question: Is there safe water and a place for children to wash hands?
items.action: Check whether children can wash hands after using the toilet and before eating.
items.warning: Lack of safe water and handwashing facilities is a health risk.
items.source_label: BRMS on hygiene, water and sanitation

items.question: Are classrooms, play spaces and feeding areas clean?
items.action: Observe the cleanliness of floors, mats, toys, cups, plates, sleeping areas and play materials.
items.warning: Bad smells, dirty feeding spaces, unsafe waste or visibly unclean rooms should be addressed.
items.source_label: BRMS on health, hygiene and safe learning environments

items.question: Are feeding arrangements safe and hygienic?
items.action: Ask how food is prepared, served, supervised and communicated to parents.
items.warning: Unsupervised meals, unsafe food handling or unclear feeding arrangements can put children at risk.
items.source_label: ECCE Policy and BRMS linkages to nutrition and wellbeing

items.question: Does the centre keep parent contacts and know what to do in an emergency?
items.action: Confirm that the centre has your contact, alternative contacts and a clear emergency procedure.
items.warning: A centre that cannot quickly contact parents during illness, injury or emergencies is not prepared.
items.source_label: BRMS on emergency preparedness and child wellbeing

items.question: Do children learn through play, songs, stories, movement and age-appropriate activities?
items.action: Look for play materials, story time, songs, outdoor play and child-friendly learning activities.
items.warning: Very young children sitting silently for long periods or being forced into formal academic work may not be receiving age-appropriate care.
items.source_label: ECCE Policy guidance on play-based early learning

items.question: Are play and learning materials safe for young children?
items.action: Check whether toys and materials are clean, not sharp, not choking hazards and suitable for age.
items.warning: Broken, dirty, sharp or unsafe objects used as play materials should be removed.
items.source_label: BRMS and ECCE Standards on learning materials

items.question: Are parents allowed to ask questions and receive updates about their child?
items.action: Ask how often the centre communicates with parents about attendance, wellbeing, learning and concerns.
items.warning: A centre that discourages parent questions or blocks reasonable visits should be treated with caution.
items.source_label: ECCE Policy provisions on parent and community engagement

items.question: Do children appear safe, engaged and comfortable?
items.action: Observe whether children seem fearful, withdrawn, unattended, distressed or unusually quiet around adults.
items.warning: Repeated fear, distress, unexplained injuries or sudden behaviour changes should be followed up immediately.
items.source_label: ECCE Policy on child wellbeing, protection and nurturing care

items.question: Does the centre manage child arrival and pick-up safely?
items.action: Ask who is allowed to pick children, how this is recorded and how strangers are handled.
items.warning: Children released without checking the caregiver or parent is a serious safety risk.
items.source_label: BRMS on safety, security and centre management

items.question: Are children with disabilities or additional needs welcomed and supported respectfully?
items.action: Ask how the centre supports children who need extra help, assistive support or referral.
items.warning: Refusal, stigma, isolation or neglect of children with additional needs is unacceptable.
items.source_label: ECCE Policy principles on inclusion and equity

items.question: Are rest, sleep and personal care routines safe and supervised?
items.action: Ask where children rest, who supervises them and how hygiene is maintained.
items.warning: Unsupervised sleeping areas, overcrowding or unsafe bedding can put children at risk.
items.source_label: BRMS on health, care routines and safe environments

items.question: If transport is provided, is it safe and supervised?
items.action: Ask who transports children, how attendance is checked and whether children are supervised during movement.
items.warning: Unsupervised transport or unclear pick-up/drop-off arrangements are serious safety concerns.
items.source_label: ECCE Standards on child safety and movement

items.question: Do you feel comfortable leaving your child at this centre after asking questions and observing?
items.action: Trust your observations. Ask more questions, speak to other parents and seek guidance if something feels unsafe.
items.warning: A parent’s concern should be taken seriously, especially where a child’s safety or wellbeing may be affected.
items.source_label: ECCE Policy emphasis on parent engagement and child wellbeing
